rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wāqiʿa means an event that has occurred and whose occurrence is certain; with the definite article it names the Resurrection because it is sure to come.
rows.anchor: esasen vukū‘a gelen, vukū‘u muhakkak olan hâdise demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is an adverbial expression that contains a conditional sense.
rows.anchor: اِذَا şart mânasını mutazammın zarfiyedir.

rows.speaker: مفسرون كثيرون
rows.claim: Many exegetes take the answer to the conditional as omitted for awe, yielding the sense, What tremendous things will happen when Resurrection comes.
rows.anchor: Çokları cevâbın tehvil için mahzuf olup hâsıl-ı mâna

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the apparent construction in which verse 2 supplies the answer to the conditional in verse 1.
rows.anchor: zâhir olan cevap şudur: {لَيْسَ لِوَقْعَتِهَا كَاذِبَةٌ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One rendering says no person will call the Resurrection’s occurrence false.
rows.anchor: Vak‘asına yalan diyen nefis yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, nothing false attaches to its occurrence.
rows.anchor: Yahut onun vak‘asına yalan yoktur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wuqūʿ means falling; waqʿa is the noun for one forceful fall, later used for a great blow or crisis and sometimes specifically for war.
rows.anchor: düşmek demek olduğu gibi, esasen “vak‘a” da masdar binâ-i merre olarak şiddetle bir düşüş demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People may deny Resurrection before it comes, but once it occurs no one can deny it; all must affirm it and cannot escape its impact and upheaval.
rows.anchor: kıyamet kopmadan evvel onu tekzib ve inkâr edenler bulunursa da onun vukū‘u tahakkuk edip bir kere olacak oldu mu artık onu kimse inkâr edemez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The event lowers some and raises others, as upheavals and revolutions topple states, abase the mighty, and elevate the lowly.
rows.anchor: Birtakımlarını düşürür alçaltır, diğer birtakımlarını kaldırır yükseltir; çünkü devletler yıkan fitneler, ihtilâller, inkılâblar gibi büyük vak‘alar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lowering is mentioned first either to intensify awe or because destruction precedes rebuilding in such events.
rows.anchor: takdîmi tehvil için yahut bu gibi vâkı‘ada yıkım yapıya mukaddem olduğu içindir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening conditional may replace the later when the earth is shaken, depicting it; alternatively it attaches to khāfiḍa and rāfiʿa through tanāzuʿ.
rows.anchor: bedel olarak onu bir nevi tasvirdir, yahut

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rajja means an earthquake, violent motion, or shaking, like the Turkish expression that the world has been displaced.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains are pulverized and scattered until the mountains become a mirage, as described in al-Nabaʾ 78:20; they become airborne particles.
rows.anchor: dağlar da toz duman olup bir serpiliş serpildiği

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwājan thalāthatan means three pairs, that is, three classes.
rows.anchor: siz de üç çift, yani üç sınıf olduğunuz zaman.

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: The address can encompass all humanity, present and former communities together, by way of taghlīb.
rows.anchor: Hitab tağlib suretiyle ümmet-i hâzıra ve ümem-i sâlife mecmû‘u bütün insanlara olabilirse de

rows.speaker: author

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maymana can mean the right side or arm, a place of honor in gatherings, or blessing and good fortune; its people are honored, dignified, useful, and blessed.
rows.anchor: yemin yeri, yani sağ kol, sağ taraf yahut meymenet, yümn ü bereket mânalarına gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The amazed repetition points to both senses of maymana; he takes the unmatched blessing of these people as a hint that the address concerns the present community.
rows.anchor: {مَآ أَصْحَٰبُ ٱلْمَيْمَنَةِ} Amma ne ashâb-ı meymene yani öyle çok meymenet sâhibi zatlar ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mashʾama means the left side or place of ill fortune, opposite to yumn; its people are low and worthless or bring misfortune on themselves and their kin.
rows.anchor: sol kol, yahut “yümn”ün zıddı olan şeâmet ve uğursuzluk mânalarına gelir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated exclamation signals both the left-side and ill-omen meanings of the group’s name.
rows.anchor: İki mânaya işâreten de şu vasıf tekrar olunuyor:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foremost are those who lead in worship, faith, obedience, and good works; examples include prophets, the Yasin companion, Pharaoh’s believing relative, and the earliest Companions among the emigrants and Helpers.
rows.anchor: Hakk’a kullukta iman ve tâatte hayır yarışlarında en öne geçenlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated term is subject and predicate: the true fore-runners bear the title in reality and reach the destination before the other two classes.
rows.anchor: unvânını hâiz olanlar hakikaten sâbikūn vasfını hâiz olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These are the people brought near to God and granted the highest rank and station in His presence.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ indinde yakınlığa, en yüksek mertebe ve makāma erdirilmiş zatlardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In gardens of bliss, the brought-near enjoy unending, pure spiritual and bodily pleasures.
rows.anchor: rûhânî ve cismânî nimetlerle lezzet-i dâime ve sâfiye içinde mütena‘‘imdirler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the address is to the present community, most foremost believers being from earlier generations is fitting, especially the earliest Companions; if it covers all nations, earlier people include all prophets and messengers.
rows.anchor: Sâbikūnun çoğu evvelînden olmak yaraşır. Nitekim sâbikūn-ı evvelûn ashâbdandır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thulla means a company, specifically a large company.
rows.anchor: “Sülle” cemaat, çok bir cemaat.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surur is the plural of sarīr, a throne, chair, or pavilion; mawḍūna means jewelled or inlaid with gold, pearls, rubies, and diamonds, or arranged in neat close rows.
rows.anchor: “serîr”in cem‘i, “serîr” taht ve sandalye ve köşk demektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mukhalladun can mean servants who remain youthful forever, or boys adorned with a type of earring called khilada.
rows.anchor: Dâima vildân şeklinde taze kalan genç hizmetçiler, garsonlar; yahut “hılede” denilen bir nevi küpe ile küpeli uşaklar.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Akwāb are vessels without handles or spouts; abārīq have handles and spouts; kaʾs is a full cup; maʿīn is drink flowing from a spring.
rows.anchor: Küpler sapı ve emziği olmayan sürahi, desti ve küp gibi kaplar {وَأَبَارِيقَ} ibrikler emziği ve sapı olan kaplar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not suffer headaches from the drink; alternatively, their gatherings are not disrupted and their pleasure is not cut short.
rows.anchor: Yahut cemiyetleri perişan edilmez, lezzetleri kesilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They do not lose their reason or become drunk; alternatively, their drink is never used up or brought to an end.
rows.anchor: Sarhoş olmazlar, yahut içtikleri tükenip bitirilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Protecting oneself and family from the Fire means guarding them against sins and temptations that lead there and directing them to God’s commands and obedience.
rows.anchor: cehennem ateşine sürüklenmelerine sebep olacak fitne ve isyandan koruyarak Allah’ın emirlerine, tâate sevkedin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A household head is accountable for both himself and his family, as expressed by two well-known Prophetic hadiths about shepherding and being best to one’s family.
rows.anchor: aile sâhibi kendinden mes’ul olduğu gibi ailesinden de mes’uldür.

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports that Umar asked the Messenger how people could protect their families; the Prophet replied to forbid them what God forbids and command them what He commands.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ömer “yâ Resûlullah! Nefislerimizi vikāye ederiz, fakat ehillerimizi nasıl vikāye edebiliriz?” demişti

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: Al-Kashshaf records a report urging the family to keep up prayer, fasting, zakat, and care for the poor, orphans, and neighbors, hoping God will gather them in Paradise.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf’ta da şu hadisleri kayd eylemiştir:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children are included in ahl; some also include them in anfus because a child is a part of its father.
rows.anchor: “Evlâd” “ehil”de dâhildir. Bazıları da “enfüs”te dâhil demişlerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fire’s fuel of people and stones is also stated in al-Baqara 2:24.
rows.anchor: yakacağı o insanlar ve o taşlardır (Sûre-i Bakara’da

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The harsh, powerful angels assigned to the Fire are called zabāniya; their severity is directed at Hell’s inhabitants because God commanded it.
rows.anchor: Ki bunlara “zebânî” denilir. Bunların gılzatları ve şiddetleri ehl-i cehenneme karşıdır.

words: لَّا يَعْصُونَ ٱللَّهَ مَآ أَمَرَهُمْ وَيَفْعَلُونَ مَا يُؤْمَرُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All angels obey God without opposition and carry out whatever they are commanded.
rows.anchor: Onlarda Allah’ın emrine isyan ve muhalefet olmaz, kendilerine her ne emrolunursa onu icrâ ederler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After this warning, the discourse turns to address the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: sonra kâfirlere hitâben şöyle buyuruluyor:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At pause Nūn has sukūn; in connected recitation most readers pronounce it with izhār, while some assimilate it into wāw with or without ghunna.
rows.anchor: Nûn vakf üzere sâkindir. Vasıl hâlinde kıraatlerin ekserîsinde izhar ile, bazısında vâv’da gunneli veya gunnesiz idgam ile okunur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like the opening Ṭā Hā, Nūn is semantically among the ambiguous passages, though not lexically so for the author; outwardly it is the familiar letter nūn.
rows.anchor: bizim için lügaten olmasa bile mânen müteşâbihâttandır. Bunun zâhiri ص,ق gibi hurûf-i hecâdan bildiğimiz nûn harfi olmasıdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The letter’s dotted, circular form resembles an inkpot and its name begins and ends with the same sound; it is also among the most resonant speech sounds.
rows.anchor: Bir nokta ile bir hokka ve çanak gibi dâirevî bir şekilde yazılır. İsmi de evvel ve âhiri bir olan نُون lâfzıdır. Harf denilen sesler içinde en ihtizazlı bir ses olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn can point from the ordered components of creation to God, just as words and sentences are assembled from letters; as a specific letter it can also indicate the alphabet generally.
rows.anchor: kitâb-ı fıtratın nizâmında derece derece müfredât ve besâitten mürekkebât dizilerek mebde’den müntehâya vücûd-i Hakk’a delâlet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other possible allusions are the human groan and cosmic resonance, the earth-and-sky world viewed as a hemisphere, or the letter’s resemblance to an inkwell and ink.
rows.anchor: enîn-i beşerin ve tanîn-i hilkatin en ziyade mümessili olan bir ses, yahut nazarımızda bir merkeze nâzır nısf-ı küre şeklinde tecellî eden âlemin Arz ve semâsıyla

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By pointing to the origins and purpose of speech and writing, Nūn’s oath draws attention to the value of language, writing, and the people of the pen, and issues a challenge.
rows.anchor: fıtratta kelâm ve yazının menşe’ ve gayesine telvih ve bunlara kasem ile lisânın ve yazının ve ehl-i kalemin kıymetine tenbih ederek tahaddî daveti ifade eder bir harftir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nūn takes the mind from one point into the depths, inviting reflection on the letters of the revealed Book, the Book of creation, and the origin of existence.
rows.anchor: derinlere götürerek kitâb-ı münzelden kitâb-ı hilkate ve mebde’-i vücûda kadar bütün harfleri düşündürebilir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading of Nūn does not prevent the sūra from also taking its name from it.
rows.anchor: Ve böyle olması aynı zamanda sûrenin ismi olmasına da mâni‘değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Writing the symbol ن and reading it as Nūn signals that the letter itself, not its name, is intended; it is left uninflected and read at pause.
rows.anchor: müsemmâsı maksud olduğuna tenbih için ن yazılmış ve i‘rab olunmayıp vakf üzere okunmuştur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pause evokes the lament of those who lost the flowing water at the previous sūra’s end; only the Quran descending from the Merciful can soothe them, and pens should serve it.
rows.anchor: evvelki sûrenin âhirindeki mâ’-i ma‘îni kaybetmiş olanların enînleri ancak bir âb-ı revân gibi mâye-i hayat olmak üzere taraf-ı Rahmân’dan nâzil olan Kur’an ile dinlendirebileceğine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever else is intended, the apparent first meaning is the familiar letter nūn, which many exegetes also prefer; this partly resolves verbal ambiguity while semantic ambiguity remains.
rows.anchor: ن mâlumumuz bulunan nûn harfi olmak zâhir ve birçok müfessirînin muhtârı da budur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Besides the letter, Arabic nūn can mean fish, as in the reference to Jonah in al-Anbiya 21:87; it can also mean an inkpot and other things.
rows.anchor: Arabîde نُون ismi bu harften başka olarak Hazret-i Yûnus’a وَذَا ٱلنُّونِ

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some identify Nūn with the great fish Yehmūt, on which the earths rest.
rows.anchor: Bazıları demiştir ki: Nûn büyük balıktır ki arzlar

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir transmits from Ibn Abbas that God first created the Pen; its decree covered all future events, then vapor formed the heavens, Nūn was created, and the earth spread on it; its shaking led to mountains anchoring it.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr İbn Abbas’tan bu babda şunları rivayet eyler: Birincisi; Allah teâlâ’nın ilk halkettiği şey Kalem’dir.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second report from Ibn Abbas says the Pen was first, was commanded to write everything until Resurrection, and then Nūn was created on water and the earth spread over it.
rows.anchor: Bir diğeri: “Rabbimin ilk halkettiği şey Kalem’dir.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alusi transmits an Ibn Abbas hadith through Ziya and others; al-Hakim grades it authentic, and it says earth spread over Nūn, its convulsion shook earth, and mountains stabilized it before Ibn Abbas recited this verse.
rows.anchor: ve Hâkim’in sahih diye ve daha birtakımlarının İbn Abbas’tan rivayet eyledikleri bir hadis olmak üzere şöyle nakletmiştir

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid’s report calls the supporting Nūn a fish, which made that description popular; the author says it is not an ordinary fish and warns against mistaken inferences.
rows.anchor: Fakat Mücâhid’den rivayette buna Arz’ın veya arzların üzerinde bulunduğu hût tâbir edilmiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reconciles the reports as a creation sequence: the Pen of decree is a spiritual first principle, called by some the First Intellect or Muhammadan Light, followed by matter and cosmic bodies formed from vapor.
rows.anchor: İbtidâ Kalem-i A‘lâ denilen ve takdîr-i ezelîde kıyamete kadar cereyan edecek şeylerin bir projesini yapan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth’s spherical liquid material separated from the heavens and was called Nūn or Hūt; later its crust formed as a shell spread over that sphere.
rows.anchor: ki “fezâ” dediğimiz semâ deryâsında yüzen bu maddeye kürevî olduğu anlatılmak üzere

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As the crust enclosed the liquid core, its constrained convulsions caused earthquakes, cracks, and volcanoes; accumulated earth waves formed mountains that stabilized the planet, as reflected by the Quranic term awtād, pegs.
rows.anchor: o Nûn evvelkisi gibi teneffüs edemeyerek nefesi tıkanmış bir balık gibi ıztırap ile deprenmeye başladığından bu sebeple hareket-i Arz, yani zelzeleler husûle gelmeye

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mountain formation greatly benefited life; earthquakes, subsidence, volcanoes, and new or collapsing mountains still occur, but are minor compared with the earliest period and do not make the earth uninhabitable.
rows.anchor: Dağların teşekkülünün bu suretle Arz üzerinde hayat için büyük fâideleri olmuş ve bundan dolayı onların Arz’a karşı tefâhürle yukarıdan bakmaya bir hakları vardır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth and mountains could suddenly disintegrate into scattered dust, as will be described in Sūrat al-Hāqqa; the author considers such an event possible at any time.
rows.anchor: bir lahzada un gibi dağılıp hebâen mensûrâ edilivermesi de her gün ihtimal dâhilindedir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Present earthquakes, subsidence, and volcanoes are movements of the Nūn by God’s command; fissures, eruptions, depressions, mountains, hills, and plains are lines written by the Supreme Pen.
rows.anchor: vukū‘bulmakta olan zelzeleler, hasifler, volkanlar dahi demek ki hep Arz’ın altındaki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues that contemporary geological conclusions about the earth’s formation, mountains, and earthquakes amount to the same account given by these reports.
rows.anchor: zamanımızda Arz’ın teşekkülü ve dağların tekevvünü ve zelzelelerin tehaddüsü hakkında fen nâmına

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People on both sides mock the fish and geological accounts without understanding one another, sometimes branding each other ignorant or unbelieving; both err by forgetting that God commands the process.
rows.anchor: iki tarafta da bunun Allah’ın emriyle olmasını unutandır ki cehalet eder.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some commentaries call the earth’s central sphere Hūt-i Aʿẓam or Yehmūt; some read Behmūt, but Qadi’s gloss specifies Yehmūt, with an alternative vowel pattern suggesting an intensive form.
rows.anchor: Bunu bâ ile mübhemiyetten “Behmût” okuyanlar olmuş ise de Kâdî hâşiyelerinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He derives Yehmūt from words for madness, raging attackers such as a flood or camel, and the boundless desert or severe famine; it can then denote volcano or space and the earth’s imprisoned, compressed, eruptive core.
rows.anchor: “Yehem” cünun; “eyhemân” iki saldırıcı ki bedeviler sel ile adama saldıran kızgın esrik deveye, medenîler de sel ile yangına derler.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names describe different aspects: Yehmūt’s severity and terror, Hūt’s convulsion, and Nūn’s groan or circular rotation around the center.
rows.anchor: içine şiddet ve dehşeti itibariyle “Yehemût”, ıztırâbı itibariyle “Hût”, iniltisi veya merkez etrafında istidâresi itibariyle de “Nûn” denilmiş demek olur.

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Some exegetes, relying on the reports, take Nūn as an oath by the fish, meaning Yehmūt.
rows.anchor: Bir kısım müfessirîn zikrolunan rivayetlere binâen burada “Nûn”, hût, yani balık mânasına

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: Other exegetes identify the Nūn with Jonah’s fish: al-Qalam calls Jonah the companion of the fish, al-Anbiya calls him Dhū al-Nūn, and al-Saffat says the fish swallowed him.
rows.anchor: Bir kısmı da sûrede فَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ وَلَا تَكُن كَصَاحِبِ ٱلْحُوتِ إِذْ نَادَىٰ وَهُوَ مَكْظُومٌۭ buyurulmuş olması
